key_insight: Nearly half of pregnancies in this EHR cohort had stigmatizing language in their clinical notes, suggesting bias in obstetric documentation is common and measurable.
clinical_relevance: Monitoring note language with NLP could help health systems identify and reduce documentation bias that may differ by race, education, and pregnancy outcomes.
method: Keyword-guided BERT classifier for stigmatizing language detection
Compared stigma prevalence and adjusted odds across demographic and clinical groups
evidence_signal: The study used a large single-center cohort and found stigma in 47% of pregnancies, with significant adjusted associations for Black race, lower maternal education, and preterm birth categories.
watch_item: Results come from one academic medical center and a classifier-based text screen, so generalizability and possible labeling/classification errors need validation before operational use.
paper_title: Forty-seven percent of pregnancies have stigmatizing language in their clinical notes in an electronic health record cohort
